title: Recording Field Observations
description: This SOP covers the process of recording field observations in SeaFoundry, including general observations, health assessments, biofouling, disease documentation, and photo evidence capture. Proper observation recording is essential for tracking organism health over time and making data-driven restoration decisions.

steps.title: Accessing the Observation Dialog
steps.description: Observations can be recorded at multiple levels: Site, Group (Structure), or individual Organism. Navigate to the desired level in the hierarchy, then look for the floating action button (FAB) in the bottom-right corner. The action dock provides quick access to observation types. Tap the observation icon (eye symbol) to open the observation menu, then select the appropriate observation type: General, Health, Biofouling, Pest, Disease, Discoloration, Thermal Stress, or Maintenance Required.

steps.title: Unified Observation Dialog Overview
steps.description: The Unified Observation Dialog (UnifiedObservationDialog) adapts its fields based on the observation type selected. At the top of the dialog, you will see: the dialog title with an icon indicating the observation type, an Organism Selector to switch between organism kinds (fields change based on selection), and the 'Apply to' target selector. The form fields below change dynamically based on your selected observation type.

steps.title: Selecting Observation Targets
steps.description: The 'Apply to' section uses the ObservationTargetSelector component. By default, the observation applies to the node you launched the dialog from. To apply the same observation to multiple targets (e.g., all organisms showing similar symptoms), tap 'Select additional structures or corals' to expand the target selector. Check the boxes next to additional structures or organisms. This is efficient for recording the same health issue across multiple specimens.

steps.title: Health Observation Fields
steps.description: When recording a Health Issue observation (ObservationDialogType.healthIssue), complete the following fields:
checklistItems: Health Issue Type: Select from dropdown (biofouling, pest, disease, discoloration, thermal stress, etc.)
Create Task toggle: Enable if follow-up action is needed - this will prompt you to create a linked task after saving
Comment: Add detailed notes about the observation, including visual indicators and any context
Evidence: Optionally capture a photo using the 'Capture Photo' button

steps.title: Biofouling Observation Fields
steps.description: When recording a Biofouling observation (ObservationDialogType.biofouling), complete the following fields:
checklistItems: Biofouling Type: Select the type of fouling organism (algae, tunicates, sponges, etc.)
Severity: Rate as mild, moderate, or severe using the dropdown
Location: Describe where on the organism or structure the biofouling is located
Cleaning Performed: Toggle on if cleaning was completed during this visit
Comment: Additional notes about the biofouling condition and any treatments applied

steps.title: Disease Observation Fields
steps.description: When recording a Disease observation (ObservationDialogType.disease), complete the following fields:
checklistItems: Disease Type: Select from the disease type dropdown (SCTLD, White Band, Black Band, etc.)
Severity: Rate the severity level using the dropdown
Affected Percentage: Enter the estimated percentage of tissue affected (numeric field)
Treatment Initiated: Toggle on if treatment has been started
Comment: Document disease progression, visual symptoms, and any treatment details

steps.title: Capturing Photo Evidence
steps.description: The Evidence section at the bottom of the observation dialog allows you to attach photographic documentation. Tap 'Capture Photo' to open the camera interface. If camera permissions have not been granted, you will be prompted to allow camera access. After capturing, the filename appears below the button. Use 'Remove' to discard and retake if needed. Photos are uploaded to cloud storage when the observation is saved and linked to the observation record for future reference.

steps.title: Saving the Observation
steps.description: Review all entered information before saving. Required fields must be completed for the Save button to become active. Tap 'Save' to record the observation. If you enabled 'Create Task' for a health observation, the Task Event Dialog will automatically open next, pre-populated with relevant information from your observation. The observation is then propagated to parent nodes (group, site, organization) for aggregate reporting and appears in activity feeds.

steps.title: Editing Existing Observations
steps.description: To edit a previously recorded observation, navigate to the observation in the activity feed or observation history. Observations can be corrected by opening the edit dialog, which pre-fills all previously entered values. When editing, a 'Correction Notes' field may appear to document why the observation was modified. Note that original observation timestamps are preserved; only the content is updated along with an updated timestamp.

steps.title: Image Observation (Orthomosaic Upload)
steps.description: For comprehensive visual documentation, the Image Observation Dialog (ImageObservationDialog) supports larger image uploads. This is separate from the Unified Observation Dialog and is used for:
checklistItems: Orthomosaic images of structures or sites

steps.title: Observation Best Practices
steps.description: Always verify you are recording observations against the correct organism or structure before saving. Use consistent terminology in comments to enable better searchability. When documenting disease or thermal stress, include environmental context if known (recent temperature spikes, storm events, etc.). Take photos from consistent angles to enable time-series comparisons. If connectivity is poor, observations are queued locally and sync when connection is restored - do not close the app until sync completes.
